description: Alma Schellart and colleagues at the University of Sheffield report analysis of open annual combined-sewer-overflow spill frequency and duration records from England and Wales. They examine associations with physical and socioeconomic factors, finding some correlation with rainfall and catchment steepness while reporting difficulty explaining spill duration. The report also compares CSO monitoring and regulation across ten European countries or regions and discusses implications for sustainable drainage assets. Coverage is the observed England/Wales database and the stated European policy comparison, not a simulated forecast of future spills. Zenodo supplies the report freely under CC BY 4.0. Exact database years, statistical equations and analysis-code access are unspecified. Related conference papers describe the same research questions. A limitation is that correlations do not establish causes or receiving-water harm, and neither raw spill records nor the report body was obtained.
